title: Testing grain size dependent variability of cosmogenic nuclide concentrations for dating fluvial sediment
author: Ruszkiczay-Rüdiger, Csillag, et al.

steps.title: Collect bulk sediment samples
steps.instruction: In 2021 collect ~3 kg of bulk sediment from two quarry levels: lower level at ~13 ± 2 m depth (sample Kem21‑03) and upper level at ~8 ± 2 m depth (sample Kem21‑04). Record that no hiatus or unconformity is observed between the horizons.

steps.title: Separate grain‑size fractions
steps.instruction: Sieve each bulk sample to obtain the following grain‑size fractions: from the lower level 0.25–0.5 mm, 1–2 mm, 4–8 mm, and 40–60 mm; from the upper level 0.25–0.5 mm, 1–2 mm, and 10–20 mm. Retain ~0.2–0.5 kg of sand and small‑pebble fractions (0.25–0.5 mm and 1–2 mm) and ~0.5 kg of the largest 4–6 cm pebbles (≈15 quartz/quartzite pebbles, representing 6–7 % of total weight).

steps.title: Crush and re‑sieve larger fractions
steps.instruction: For grain‑size fractions larger than 1 mm, crush the material and sieve again, retaining the 0.5–1.0 mm fraction for subsequent chemical processing.

steps.title: Prepare samples chemically
steps.instruction: Process all selected fractions in the Cosmogenic Nuclide Sample Preparation Laboratory (HUN‑REN, CSFK, Budapest) following the procedures of Merchel & Herpers (201X) and Merchel et al. (201X) as described in Ruszkiczay‑Rüdiger et al. [36].

steps.title: Determine stable 27Al
steps.instruction: Measure stable 27Al concentrations by Microwave Plasma‑Atom Emission Spectrometry using an Agilent 4100 MP‑AES at the Institute of Nuclear Research (Debrecen, Hungary).

steps.title: Measure 10Be and 26Al by AMS
steps.instruction: Send the chemically prepared samples to the Vienna Environmental Research Accelerator (VERA, University of Vienna) for accelerator mass spectrometry measurement of 10Be and 26Al isotopic ratios.

steps.title: Calculate burial ages (isochron)
steps.instruction: Perform isochron burial age calculations using χ²‑fitting inverse modelling as described by Ruszkiczay‑Rüdiger et al. [18], applying a user‑defined upper threshold for sink denudation rate of 50 m Ma⁻¹.

steps.title: Identify and remove outliers
steps.instruction: Assess the dataset for potential outliers using a reduced χ² test, bootstrap resampling, and evaluation of pre‑ vs. post‑burial CRN inventories; omit samples flagged as outliers (e.g., Kem21‑03A, Kem21‑03C, Kem21‑04B) before final age determination.

steps.title: Report final burial age and rates
steps.instruction: Report the most probable burial age, sink denudation rate, and apparent source denudation rates (e.g., 3.92 ± 0.69 Ma, 20.4 ± 3.2 m Ma⁻¹, 13–16 ± 2–4 m Ma⁻¹) together with the reduced χ² value of the final model fit.
